text:
mira: Heads-up — I pushed a short proposal for audit schema changes around tenant-scoped events. Need to ensure member-only events never show up in org-admin/customer exports. Proposed field: `visibility` enum on events. thoughts?

jon: +1 on explicit enum. Suggest values: `tenant_member`, `tenant_admin`, `org_admin`, `system`, `public`. Keep it small and deterministic.

alex: SRE concern: schema bump impacts consumers (log-aggregator, export-service, analytics). We need migration strategy. Version header or topic versioning?

mira: Agreed. Plan A: include `audit-version: 2` header on new messages and keep v1 payload around for 30 days. Consumers should tolerate unknown fields.

kira: Compliance note: customer-facing exports must have stable semantics. If we change visibility logic, we need a mapping layer that translates internal visibility to what the customer can view (e.g., members vs admins).

sam: Product question — for token lifecycle events, members should never see other members' tokens in the export. How do we redact safely?

mira: Redaction plan: events have `actor`, `target`, `details`. Add `redaction_mask` array that tags fields as `sensitive`. At export time, map viewer role -> allowed fields. Eg members get `details: {action: "rotate", metadata: {}}` with token strings removed.

jon: Implementation detail: do RBAC checks at the export-service boundary. Do not rely on downstream consumers. Use scoped token claims like `scopes: ["audit:read:tenant:<tenant_id>"]` and also check `viewer_role` claim.

audit-bot: deploy notice: audit-service v1.9.2 -> v2.0.0 canary starting now :rocket:

alex: For rollout, add a fallback stream to the v1 topic if any export fails during canary. Also add an integration test simulating cross-tenant export attempts.

mira: vuln triage: found an access vector where scoped tokens could call the internal `/audit/query` endpoint via a proxy without proper header checks. We should patch the header validation and add gating checks for `x-internal-call`.

jon: Working on PR #8423 that enforces `x-internal-call` and validates `audit-version` header. Adding unit tests for visibility matrix. Will also add an integration test that spins up export-service + aggregator.

kira: KMS question: who signs export manifests? For private deployments we must sign with customer KMS; for hosted we sign with Redwood KMS but include the signing key id and chain. Need spec for both.

mira: Proposal: export envelope includes `manifest` + `signature`. For private, signature created by customer KMS; for hosted, Redwood signs but we include `redwood-signature` and a `signed-by` field. Verification steps documented in export API.

sam: UX ask: add event `export.downloaded_by` containing `actor_role`, `actor_id`, `destination` (S3/email) so customers can see who pulled exports.

alex: Also flag: retention enforcement must use `visibility` field. Legal retention windows differ by event visibility. Make sure retention manager queries `visibility` not `actor_role`.

jon: Quick checklist of action items: 
  1) Define `visibility` enum + docs and wire into events (mira/jon)
  2) Add `audit-version` header and version negotiation strategy (jon)
  3) Migration plan + canary + fallback stream (alex)
  4) RBAC checks in export-service + scoped token tests (jon)
  5) KMS signing spec for private/hosted exports (mira/kira)
  6) Redaction rules and redaction_mask mapping doc (sam)
  7) Patch scoped-token internal API hole + integration tests (jon)

mira: I'll open a DESIGN doc with a diagram and add the visibility matrix. Will link in thread when ready.

kira: I'll prepare a compliance checklist and customer-facing export guarantees to attach to the DESIGN doc.

sam: Thanks — please @-mention me when the redaction rules draft is up. :thumbsup:

jon: FYI I'll land the header validation PR behind a feature flag so we can roll it to canary first.

mira: Good. I'll also schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to run through edge cases (cross-tenant reads, export-of-exports, delegated admin).

alex: Adding runbook snippet: if post-migration we see "permission_denied" spikes, rollback consumer to v1 and pause canary.

mira: closing loop — priority: patch scoped-token hole (hotfix), then schema design. I'll post links here shortly.

kira: ack.

sam: Thanks everyone.
